title: faBolus phone↔remote command contract
description: The tiny message contract shared by the iOS host and its remotes (Apple Watch over WatchConnectivity, Garmin over the Connect IQ mobile SDK). Both the Swift side and the Monkey C side validate/generate against this. Keep it minimal — this is safety-critical surface. DRAFT: finalize during Milestone 2.

version.description: Schema version. Bump on any breaking change; both sides must match.

kind.description: Command type. suspendPump/resumePump are remote advanced-control requests; the phone re-confirms them on-device before executing and only honors them when advanced control is enabled for a Mobi.

requestId.description: Client-generated unique id correlating a request → confirm → status across the phone↔watch hop.

sentAt.description: Immutable send-time stamp (Unix seconds), set once by the sender when it composes a pump-mutating command. The host computes now − sentAt at receipt and refuses a DELIVERY-AUTHORIZING command (bolusRequest/bolusConfirm/resumePump) that is too old to apply safely — a bolus queued or retransmitted minutes late is a double-dose hazard. Insulin-REDUCING commands (cancelBolus/suspendPump) are never freshness-gated, so refusing a late safety action can't happen. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec: watchOS Int and Monkey C Lang.Number are signed 32-bit. Absent ⇒ a legacy sender predating the field (not rejected).

units.description: Insulin units to deliver (bolusRequest). Milestone 2 is units-only.

carbsGrams.description: Optional carbs for the calculator flow (Milestone 2 follow-on). Absent = units-only.

bgMgdl.description: Optional BG for the calculator flow (Milestone 2 follow-on).

remoteEstimateUnits.description: The dose the remote computed/showed for a carb bolusRequest. The host recomputes authoritatively from carbsGrams and rejects the bolus if the two diverge beyond its safety limit (stale-settings guard). Absent for a units-only request.

includeStaleBG.description: bolusRequest (remote → host, Addendum B) — the remote's per-attempt intent to INCLUDE a stale-but-real CGM reading in the correction on a carb bolus; insulin-increasing. Set true ONLY when the user explicitly chose to include the stale reading for THIS attempt (never sticky, never on a fresh reading); absent otherwise. The host honors it only when it can recompute from its own matching stale reading; absent (and on any legacy host that ignores the field) the host fails closed to a carbs-only dose. Meaningful only on a carb/correction request, never a units-mode one.

forceGlucose.description: On a statusRead, asks the host to force a fresh CGM read from the pump before replying. A remote sets this when opening its bolus screen so the shown estimate is off the newest value.

confirmToken.description: Opaque token issued by the host for a specific bolusRequest; echoed by the remote in bolusConfirm to complete the double-confirmation. Single-use, short-lived.

status.description: Delivery/connection status echoed back to the remote (bolusStatus). 'unknown' (FB-02) = the pump outcome is genuinely indeterminate (initiate written but no confirmation) — the remote must NOT claim delivered/failed; it points the user to pump/t:connect history.

deliveredUnits.description: Units actually delivered so far (bolusStatus) — important for partial-delivery after a cancel.

message.description: Optional human-readable detail for display on the remote.

trend.description: Glucose trend direction token. Remotes draw their own arrow shape from this; their fonts can't render Unicode arrows.

carbRatio.description: Pump's carb ratio (grams per unit), shared so a remote can compute carbs→units locally (statusRead reply).

isf.description: Pump's insulin sensitivity factor (mg/dL per unit) for local correction calc (statusRead reply).

targetBg.description: Pump's correction target (mg/dL) for local correction calc (statusRead reply).

maxBolusUnits.description: Pump's configured max bolus (units) — governs the remote's UI cap (statusRead reply).

reservoirUnits.description: Insulin units remaining in the reservoir (statusRead reply, for a remote's detail screen).

batteryPercent.description: Pump battery percent (statusRead reply, for a remote's detail screen).

lastBolusUnits.description: Units of the most recent bolus (statusRead reply, for a remote's detail screen).

basalRate.description: Current basal delivery rate (units/hr), so a remote's basal pill matches the host (statusRead reply). Absent means the pump has never answered the basal read; a real 0 U/hr (a 0 U/hr temp rate, or a suspend) still travels as 0 — that distinction is why the host gates emission on having read the rate at all, rather than sending 0 for both cases.

glucoseEpochSec.description: Immutable source timestamp of the current CGM reading (Unix seconds), set once at origin from the pump's own reading time and propagated unchanged through every hop. A receiver computes age as now - glucoseEpochSec at display time. When absent, the reading's age is UNKNOWN and must render as stale/no-data, never as fresh. The maximum is Int32.max (2038-01-19) because that is the widest value every consumer can represent: Int is 32-bit on watchOS (arm64_32) and Monkey C's Lang.Number is a signed 32-bit integer. Widening requires Int64 in faBolusCore, Lang.Long on Garmin, and this maximum, changed together.

iobEpochSec.description: DIF-ux — immutable source timestamp (Unix seconds) of the active-insulin (IOB, op-109) read the host relayed, set once at origin from the pump's own read time. A remote computes age as now - iobEpochSec at display time to grey/age its IOB row and PRE-WARN before a bolus. When absent the IOB age is UNKNOWN and must render as stale (never fresh) — the same rule as glucoseEpochSec, and the same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling because Int is 32-bit on watchOS and Monkey C's Lang.Number is signed 32-bit. Remotes only view/pre-warn on this; the host stays the authoritative dose gate.

therapyEpochSec.description: DIF-ux — immutable source timestamp (Unix seconds) of the therapy-params (carb ratio / ISF / target, op-115) read the host relayed. A remote computes age as now - therapyEpochSec to grey/age its carb-ratio/ISF/target rows and PRE-WARN. Absent ⇒ age UNKNOWN ⇒ render stale, never fresh. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec (32-bit watchOS Int / Monkey C Lang.Number). View/pre-warn only on remotes; the host stays the authoritative dose gate.

reservoirEpochSec.description: Immutable source timestamp (Unix seconds) of the reservoir (op-37 InsulinStatusResponse) read the host relayed, set once at origin from the pump's own read time and propagated unchanged. A receiver computes age as now - reservoirEpochSec at DISPLAY time (an age computed at compose time is already wrong by however long the message was in flight). Absent ⇒ the value's age is UNKNOWN and must render as stale/no-data, never as fresh; absent also covers never-read and legacy-host. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec (32-bit watchOS Int / Monkey C Lang.Number). Pairs with reservoirUnits: the wire is deliberately presence-gated, NOT freshness-gated, so it carries the value AND its age and each receiver applies its own policy. Omitting an aged value cannot decay a receiver that keeps the last value on an absent key — it only strips information from a number the receiver goes on showing.

batteryEpochSec.description: Immutable source timestamp (Unix seconds) of the pump battery (op-145 CurrentBatteryV2Response) read the host relayed, set once at origin from the pump's own read time and propagated unchanged. A receiver computes age as now - batteryEpochSec at DISPLAY time (an age computed at compose time is already wrong by however long the message was in flight). Absent ⇒ the value's age is UNKNOWN and must render as stale/no-data, never as fresh; absent also covers never-read and legacy-host. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec (32-bit watchOS Int / Monkey C Lang.Number). Pairs with batteryPercent: the wire is deliberately presence-gated, NOT freshness-gated, so it carries the value AND its age and each receiver applies its own policy. Omitting an aged value cannot decay a receiver that keeps the last value on an absent key — it only strips information from a number the receiver goes on showing.

history.description: Recent glucose values (mg/dL), oldest→newest, ~5-min spacing, for a remote history plot.

historyEpochs.description: Per-point source timestamps (Unix seconds) aligned 1:1 with `history` (same length, oldest→newest), so a remote plots each reading at its REAL time — a data gap renders as a gap, not evenly-spaced points. Absent ⇒ the remote falls back to assumed ~5-min spacing. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec: watchOS `Int` and Monkey C `Lang.Number` are signed 32-bit. (Was already emitted by the host + consumed by the Watch/Mac clients since the real-epochs fix, but undocumented here — additionalProperties is false, so document before any surface relies on it over the wire.)

alerts.description: Active pump alerts/alarms (statusRead reply) for a remote to view.

severity.description: Phase 20 (D-01): phone-classified salience tier for the Garmin alert-intensity gate. Optional; a legacy host omits it and the watch treats an absent/unknown severity as 'critical' (highest salience, never suppressed).

alertId.description: The notification id to clear (dismissAlert command).

alertKind.description: The notification kind to clear (dismissAlert command).

bolusMode.description: Default bolus entry mode a remote should honor (statusRead reply).

bolusIncrement.description: Units step for a remote's bolus entry (statusRead reply).

carbIncrement.description: Grams step for a remote's carb entry (statusRead reply).

screenOrder.description: Garmin remote swipe order (statusRead reply). Ids match AppState.ALL_SCREENS.

defaultScreen.description: Garmin remote screen shown first (statusRead reply).

glucoseStaleMinutes.description: Minutes after which a CGM reading is stale (statusRead reply): remotes de-emphasize it and stop using it for carb→unit correction, matching the phone.

glucoseHideDelayMinutes.description: Minutes after going stale to keep showing the greyed value before hiding it as '--' (statusRead reply). 0 = hide immediately when stale; omitted = never hide.

detailsOrder.description: Detail rows a remote's details screen should show, in order (statusRead reply). Hidden rows are omitted.

watchChartRanges.description: Time ranges (hours) a remote's history chart cycles through on tap (statusRead reply).

garminComplicationDisplay.description: How the Garmin BG complication presents (statusRead reply): numericColor = numeric value with range-coloring + Latin trend in the unit slot; stringTrend = a plain value+trend string, no color.

garminComplicationSlots.description: Phase 20 (F1, D-02): which pump-status fields fill the Garmin's THREE user-assignable complication slots, in order (statusRead reply). Connect IQ caps an app at 4 complications total, so glucose (fixed) + these ≤3. The watch de-dupes + caps at 3; absent/all-unknown ⇒ the watch keeps its default (iob/reservoir/battery).

watchNotificationIntents.description: The resolved per-surface WATCH notification intent for each relayed category (statusRead reply), keyed by an opaque category identifier. Source-agnostic: a value is the watch's resolved intent for that category whether the category is mirrored from the pump or generated by the app, so every watch-facing surface consumes this one field, mapping the intent to its own ladder. Each value is 'off' (nothing), 'quiet' (visual only), or 'alert' (the vibrating rung) — the watch ladder has no breakthrough/urgent rung. CONTRACT: an absent field, an absent key, or an unrecognized value means the receiver fails safe to the vibrating rung — never silent — so a legacy host that omits it can never quiet a pump safety alert. An explicit recognized value, including 'off', is the user's own choice and is honored. App-own categories ride this map under a namespaced key ('appOwn:<category>') so they never collide with a pump-mirror group of the same name.

appOwnAlerts.description: The active app-GENERATED (faBolus's own) alert subset for the watch to annunciate (statusRead reply) — the app-own analog of 'alerts' (which mirrors the pump's own alarms). Each item carries its content (a namespaced 'key' + a 'title'); its resolved per-surface WATCH intent rides 'watchNotificationIntents' under the same namespaced key. The subset includes the durable unresolved-dose record. A watch that receives an app-own alert whose intent is absent/unrecognized fails safe to the vibrating rung — never silence — and the watch ladder has no breakthrough/urgent rung. Absent means a legacy host; an empty array is the authoritative 'no active app-own alerts'.

key.description: Namespaced category identifier ('appOwn:<category>') — the watch's dedupe identity and its watchNotificationIntents lookup key.

clockAnalog.description: Whether the Garmin clock screen draws an analog face (statusRead reply): true = analog hands, false (default) = the digital readout. Mirrored from the phone, replacing the old on-watch tap toggle. Absent ⇒ the remote keeps its digital default.

remotesReadOnly.description: Read-only mode for the Apple Watch + Garmin remotes (statusRead reply): when true they hide the bolus screen/button and won't request a bolus (the host also refuses).

glucoseDisplayUnit.description: statusRead reply — the phone's active glucose display-unit setting (Phase 4), mirrored so Apple Watch/Garmin render mg/dL/mmol like the phone. Display-only; bgMgdl and every dosing field stay mg/dL regardless. Absent ⇒ the remote defaults to mgdl (legacy-safe).

glucosePlotFloor.description: statusRead reply — the phone's glucose-plot Y-axis floor, canonical mg/dL (Phase 09.13). Shared/phone-scoped: the phone group (iPhone + Mac) reads this. Display-only, never crosses into bgMgdl/dosing. Absent ⇒ the remote's built-in default.

glucosePlotCeiling.description: statusRead reply — the phone's glucose-plot Y-axis ceiling, canonical mg/dL (Phase 09.13). Shared/phone-scoped: the phone group (iPhone + Mac) reads this. Display-only, never crosses into bgMgdl/dosing. Absent ⇒ the remote's built-in default.

glucosePlotFloorSmall.description: statusRead reply — the optional small-screen (Apple Watch + Garmin) glucose-plot Y-axis floor OVERRIDE, canonical mg/dL (Phase 09.13, D-05). Read by the small-screen group only. Display-only. Absent ⇒ the small screens follow the shared glucosePlotFloor above.

glucosePlotCeilingSmall.description: statusRead reply — the optional small-screen (Apple Watch + Garmin) glucose-plot Y-axis ceiling OVERRIDE, canonical mg/dL (Phase 09.13, D-05). Read by the small-screen group only. Display-only. Absent ⇒ the small screens follow the shared glucosePlotCeiling above.

canBolus.description: statusRead reply — the host's authoritative 'may a remote start a bolus right now?' on the broadcast-safe axes: pump linked AND not mid-delivery AND remotes not read-only. A remote ANDs this with its own reachability + the entered amount's bounds. Lets a surface that can't parse `message` (Garmin, which otherwise substring-matched the localized connection string as load-bearing safety logic) gate on a semantic flag. Per-peer permission / capability / child gates stay host-enforced on the actual deliver. Absent ⇒ the remote falls back to judging from `message` + `remotesReadOnly` locally (additive/non-breaking).

bolusBlockReason.description: statusRead reply — the reason `canBolus` is false, as a stable locale-independent token (BolusBlockReason.wireToken), so a remote can show WHY its bolus affordance is disabled. Over the wire the host emits only pumpNotLinked / bolusInFlight / accessDenied (reachability + bounds are judged locally by each remote). Absent when canBolus is true or absent.

cartridgeReady.description: statusRead reply — the pump's cartridge-ready status, pushed on every reply so watch/Garmin/Mac can show cartridge state even when no bolus is being attempted; a first-class DISPLAY signal, distinct from canBolus/bolusBlockReason (which only surface the block at bolus-attempt time). Absent means a legacy remote/host predating the field — NO SIGNAL, never a fabricated 'not ready'; a remote must only treat an explicit false as 'cartridge not ready', never infer one from a missing key.

batteryCharging.description: statusRead reply — the pump's charging state (op-145 chargingStatus == 1; the on-wire semantics are unconfirmed live). Absent means a legacy host/remote that predates the field; a remote maps absent to NOT charging (fail-closed, never a fabricated charging state). Display-only, never a dose input.

supportsRemoteAlertDismiss.description: statusRead reply — whether the pump firmware actually honors a REMOTE alert dismissal (P13 capability channel). t:slim X2 silently rejects it, so on t:slim a remote's alert action only snoozes the alert locally; Mobi clears it on the pump. A remote uses this to label its alert action 'Clear' (true) vs 'Snooze' (false), matching the phone. Absent ⇒ the remote keeps its safe default (Snooze); the host stays the enforcement point on the actual dismiss.

supportsDismissAck.description: statusRead reply (CX-G-08, 14-09) — DYNAMIC pump-tied capability: true only when the phone build supports the authenticated dismissAck path AND the connected pump honors a remote dismiss (supportsRemoteAlertDismiss == true). Computed fresh every statusRead, never a constant. True (Mobi) ⇒ the watch removes a wearer-dismissed alert ONLY on a correlated authenticated dismissAck; false/absent (t:slim, or a legacy host) ⇒ the watch falls back to the filtered-statusRead reconcile so it is never stranded.

rawAlerts.description: statusRead reply (CX-G-08, 14-10) — the pump's TRUE pre-local-snooze-filter active-alert bitmap for this poll (mirrors `alerts`' item shape exactly), emitted ONLY when supportsRawAlertSnapshot is true AND the host's raw set is known (non-nil). A wearer-dismissed alert ABSENT from a PRESENT rawAlerts (including an empty []) is proof the pump itself dropped it; PRESENT means the pump still has it. Absent (nil) rawAlerts is NO-SIGNAL, never 'zero alerts'. A reconciliation oracle for the wearer's own pending dismissals only — never a display source (the displayed list stays `alerts`).

supportsRawAlertSnapshot.description: statusRead reply (CX-G-08, 14-10) — DYNAMIC pump-tied capability, the exact NEGATION of supportsDismissAck: true only when the phone build supports the raw-snapshot backstop AND the connected pump does NOT honor a remote dismiss (supportsRemoteAlertDismiss == false, e.g. t:slim X2). Computed fresh every statusRead, never a constant. The two capabilities can never both be true for the same connected pump. Emitted unconditionally (mirrors supportsDismissAck) so a Mobi reply carries false; absent ⇒ a legacy host that predates this plan.

garminBolusEnabled.description: statusRead reply (P15 §2.3) — whether bolusing from the GARMIN watch is enabled on the phone. Default OFF; a Garmin remote hides its bolus affordance unless this is true, and a cold launch with no push yet stays disabled (fail-closed). The host also refuses a Garmin deliver when false (AccessPolicy). Absent ⇒ a legacy host predating §2.3; the remote keeps its safe default (disabled).

bolusPasscodeRequired.description: statusRead reply (P15 §2.3 / C2) — signals whether a 4-digit passcode is required to confirm a remote bolus (the phone holds the salted hash; BolusPasscodeStore.isRequired). When true a Garmin remote's confirm step is the passcode entry, REPLACING the tap-sequence / two-button-hold; the entered code rides back on bolusRequest.bolusPasscode and the host verifies it (C2 wired this end-to-end: phone set-UI → this flag → bolusPasscode field → host verify). Apple Watch is exempt (wrist detection). This flag only shapes the remote UI; the host stays the enforcement point (AccessPolicy refuses a Garmin deliver with a wrong/absent code even if the remote UI skipped the prompt). Absent/false ⇒ the surface's normal confirm.

bolusPasscode.description: bolusRequest (remote → host, C2 §2.3) — the plaintext passcode the remote's user ENTERED to confirm a Garmin bolus, carried alongside units/carbsGrams. The host verifies it against the salted hash it holds (BolusPasscodeStore.verify) and refuses the bolus if wrong/absent; the watch keeps it in RAM only and never stores or verifies it. Absent ⇒ no code was entered (a legacy remote, or one where no passcode is required); the host's gate then denies iff a passcode IS required for that surface. maxLength is a loose upper bound — the store enforces exactly 4 digits — to reject an oversized string. Not persisted in the ledger.

controllerVariant.description: statusRead reply (B2 / S1+O3) — the pump's automated-controller identity (ControllerVariant, derived from the pump's own op-79 feature bits): none / controlIQ (Control-IQ) / controlIQPro (Control-IQ+). A remote reconstructs the ControllerDescriptor locally from this token and renders the auto-correction disclosure itself, so no prose crosses the wire. Display-only — never a dose input (C3). These tokens are a FROZEN contract (see ControllerVariant). Absent ⇒ a legacy host; the remote treats it as `none` and renders nothing controller-specific.

controlIQEnabled.description: statusRead reply (B2 / S1+O3) — whether the pump's Control-IQ is turned ON at runtime (PumpSnapshot.controlIQEnabled), distinct from controllerVariant (which is firmware capability/identity). The auto-correction disclosure renders only when BOTH the variant can auto-correct AND it is enabled here, so a remote needs both. Display-only. Absent ⇒ a legacy host; the remote treats it as false (renders no disclosure) — a safe, non-misleading default.

ciqZone.description: statusRead reply — the pump's live Control-IQ action zone as a FROZEN wire token (derived from op-179), mirroring controllerVariant exactly: a remote decodes the token and renders Tandem's own zone word/icon locally, no prose crosses the wire. Display-only, never a dose input. Absent means a legacy host, or the zone is unread/unmapped; the remote renders the chip/row/field absent, never a stale or fabricated word.

ciqSuspendedForLow.description: statusRead reply — whether the pump's own control-state currently attributes an active basal suspend to Control-IQ. A frozen fail-closed fact, never a rendered string. Emitted unconditionally (nil only before the first read; false is a fully-known 'not CIQ-attributed' state). Absent or false means the remote falls back to its own generic-suspend indicator, never a fabricated 'Control-IQ paused' claim.

ciqSuspendStartEpochSec.description: The immutable source epoch (Unix seconds) of the moment ciqSuspendedForLow first became true, propagated unchanged so a receiver computes elapsed time at display time. Absent means unknown / not currently attributed. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec.

lastAutoCorrectionEpochSec.description: The immutable source epoch (Unix seconds) of the most-recent Control-IQ auto-correction, propagated unchanged so a receiver computes age at display time. Display-only, never a dose input. Absent means a legacy host or no auto-correction has been seen yet — the marker renders absent, never a synthesized time. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec.

ciqLastCouldNotDeliverEpochSec.description: The immutable source epoch of the most-recent 'Control-IQ tried and couldn't deliver an automatic correction' event. Remote marker only — the full timeline stays phone-only. Absent means the marker renders absent, never a synthesized recency claim. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec.

lockoutUntilEpochSec.description: The immutable source epoch (Unix seconds) of the instant Control-IQ's automatic correction becomes available again, propagated unchanged so a receiver reverses the arithmetic and computes a lockout-remaining fraction locally — the fraction itself is never transmitted. Emitted unconditionally (nil only when there's no known auto-correction yet, the controller can't auto-correct, or the window is unknown). Absent, or a value already in the past, means the bar/ring renders absent — never a frozen bar or negative countdown. Display-only, never a dose input. Same Int32.max (2038-01-19) ceiling as glucoseEpochSec.

maxBasalUnitsPerHour.description: The pump's configured max-basal delivery limit, propagated alongside basalRate so each remote computes its own 'percent of configured max basal' readout locally — the percentage itself is never transmitted. Display-only, never a dose input. Absent or <= 0 means the readout renders absent on every surface (fail-closed: hidden, not zero/dash).

controlIQMode.description: The pump's live Sleep/Exercise activity mode (0 normal / 1 sleep / 2 exercise). Emitted unconditionally — 0 (normal) is a fully-known fact, not absent — so a stale Sleep/Exercise mode never survives past the moment the pump's own state changed. Display-only, never a dose input. Absent means a legacy host, which the remote treats as 0 (no card).
